quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Children lined up for a fire drill outside the school building"?
quests.hint: Think about when children are usually inside the school building for classes.
quests.explanation: Yes! Fire drills happen during school hours, so this is a daytime event.
quests.funFact: Fire drills help everyone practice staying calm and leaving the building safely!

quests.instruction: "A family folding laundry while a rerun plays quietly in the background" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when families usually relax together and catch up on chores in the evening.
quests.explanation: Yes! Folding laundry while relaxing with a show is often an evening or nighttime activity.
quests.funFact: Folding laundry while watching a show is a favorite way many families multitask!

quests.instruction: "A line of people waiting outside a bakery for fresh bagels" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when bakeries usually open their doors to customers.
quests.explanation: Yes! Bakeries are usually open and busy with customers in the morning.
quests.funFact: Bagels are boiled before they're baked, which gives them their chewy texture!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "The clink of a spoon against a mug as cocoa is stirred before bed"?
quests.hint: Think about the phrase 'before bed' — when does that happen?
quests.explanation: Yes! Cocoa before bed happens at night, right before sleep.
quests.funFact: A warm drink like cocoa can help some people feel relaxed and sleepy!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A city bus stopping to pick up commuters heading to their jobs". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when most people travel to their jobs.
quests.explanation: Yes! Most people commute to work during the day.
quests.funFact: Some cities have bus systems that carry millions of passengers every single day!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A cat winding between ankles, meowing for its very last meal, right as the house grows quiet". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about the word 'last' — what does that tell you about how far the day has gone?
quests.explanation: Yes! The very last meal of the day happens in the evening, as night approaches.
quests.funFact: Cats often have a strong sense of routine and know exactly when mealtime is close!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "Joggers weaving around dog walkers on a busy park path". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about when parks are usually busiest with joggers and dog walkers.
quests.explanation: Yes! Parks are typically busiest with joggers and walkers during the day.
quests.funFact: Walking a dog is a great way for both people and pets to get healthy exercise!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "The click of a leash as a dog gets one final walk around the block". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about the word 'final' — what does that tell you about how far the day has gone?
quests.explanation: Yes! A final walk of the day usually happens in the evening, before everyone settles in for the night.
quests.funFact: Many families take their dog on one last walk to help them settle down for the night!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A crowd gathering for a ribbon-cutting ceremony at a new store"?
quests.hint: Think about when a big public event like this would draw the biggest crowd.
quests.explanation: Yes! Public ceremonies like this are usually held during the day.
quests.funFact: Ribbon-cutting ceremonies are a fun tradition to celebrate something brand new opening!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A parent double-checking that the stove is off before heading upstairs"?
quests.hint: Think about when someone would be heading upstairs for the last time that day.
quests.explanation: Yes! Heading upstairs for the night is a nighttime routine.
quests.funFact: Checking the stove before bed is a smart safety habit many families follow!

quests.instruction: "A group of scouts working on badges at an outdoor meeting" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when outdoor club meetings are usually held.
quests.explanation: Yes! Outdoor scout meetings and activities are typically held during the day.
quests.funFact: Scouts can earn badges for all sorts of skills, from camping to cooking!

quests.instruction: "The soft beep of a phone charging on a nightstand" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when a phone would be placed on a nightstand to charge overnight.
quests.explanation: Yes! Phones are often plugged in to charge on a nightstand right before bed.
quests.funFact: Charging a phone overnight makes sure it's ready to use again in the morning!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "Painters touching up the lines on a freshly painted crosswalk". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when it's easiest to see and paint straight lines on the road.
quests.explanation: Yes! Painting a crosswalk clearly is easiest to do during the day.
quests.funFact: Crosswalk paint is specially made to be tough enough for cars driving over it every day!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A toothbrush holder with two brushes, freshly rinsed and dripping". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when a family usually brushes their teeth all together, right before bed.
quests.explanation: Yes! Freshly rinsed toothbrushes suggest a family just finished brushing before bed, at night.
quests.funFact: Dentists recommend replacing a toothbrush every three to four months!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A line of cars waiting at a carwash on a busy Saturday"?
quests.hint: Think about when families usually run errands like washing the car.
quests.explanation: Yes! Errands like a carwash are usually done during the day.
quests.funFact: Automatic carwashes can clean a car in just a few minutes!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A row of shoes lined up neatly by the door, the last outing of the evening finally over"?
quests.hint: Think about the phrase 'finally over' — what does that tell you about the time?
quests.explanation: Yes! An outing being 'finally over' suggests it's now evening or night.
quests.funFact: Lining shoes up by the door is a tidy habit many families use to stay organized!

quests.instruction: "A clock's short hand pointing to nine, right as the school morning begins" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when school usually starts — is it morning or late evening?
quests.explanation: Yes! School starting tells you this nine o'clock is in the morning, part of the daytime.
quests.funFact: The short hand on a clock always points to the hour, while the long hand points to the minutes!

quests.instruction: "A clock's short hand pointing to nine, right as a bedtime story begins" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when a bedtime story usually happens — is it morning or evening?
quests.explanation: Yes! A bedtime story tells you this nine o'clock is in the evening, part of the nighttime.
quests.funFact: The very same clock time can mean morning or night — it all depends on AM and PM!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "The letters 'AM' appearing on a clock right after breakfast". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about when breakfast is usually eaten.
quests.explanation: Yes! 'AM' after breakfast tells you it's still morning, part of the daytime.
quests.funFact: 'AM' stands for a Latin phrase meaning 'before midday'!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "The letters 'PM' glowing on a clock well past a late dinner". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about the phrase 'well past a late dinner' — how far into the evening is that?
quests.explanation: Yes! Well past a late dinner means it's deep into the evening, part of the nighttime.
quests.funFact: 'PM' stands for a Latin phrase meaning 'after midday'!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A calendar page marked for a picnic planned right after lunch"?
quests.hint: Think about when lunch usually happens, and what time follows it.
quests.explanation: Yes! Right after lunch is still part of the daytime.
quests.funFact: People have used calendars to plan and track days for thousands of years!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A calendar page with tomorrow's date circled, checked right before bed"?
quests.hint: Think about the phrase 'right before bed' — when does that happen?
quests.explanation: Yes! Checking the calendar right before bed happens at night.
quests.funFact: Many people check tomorrow's plans the night before, to feel prepared!

quests.instruction: "An alarm buzzing to signal the start of a busy schedule ahead" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when an alarm usually buzzes to wake someone up.
quests.explanation: Yes! An alarm usually buzzes in the morning, to start the day.
quests.funFact: The very first alarm clocks could only be set to ring at one single time!

quests.instruction: "An alarm being set carefully for the next morning's wake-up" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when someone would set an alarm for the very next day.
quests.explanation: Yes! Setting an alarm for tomorrow morning is usually done the night before.
quests.funFact: Setting an alarm the night before can help mornings feel much less rushed!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A stopwatch timing a friendly race during gym class". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when gym class usually happens during the school schedule.
quests.explanation: Yes! Gym class happens during school hours, in the daytime.
quests.funFact: Stopwatches can measure time down to a tiny fraction of a second!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A digital clock reading '11:00 PM' beside a sleeping child". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about whether 11:00 PM is closer to midday or to midnight.
quests.explanation: Yes! 11:00 PM is late in the evening, deep into the nighttime.
quests.funFact: A sleeping child's body is hard at work resting and growing, even at 11:00 PM!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A wall clock in the classroom showing it's almost time for lunch"?
quests.hint: Think about when lunchtime usually happens during the school day.
quests.explanation: Yes! Lunchtime happens in the middle of the school day, during the daytime.
quests.funFact: Many classrooms keep a clock on the wall to help everyone stay on schedule!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A grandfather clock's slow ticking, the only sound in a quiet house"?
quests.hint: Think about when a house would be quiet enough for a ticking clock to be the only sound.
quests.explanation: Yes! A completely quiet house suggests everyone is asleep, at night.
quests.funFact: Grandfather clocks got their name from a song about a clock that stopped the moment its owner passed away!

quests.instruction: "A digital clock reading '2:00 PM' as an afternoon quiz begins" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about whether 2:00 PM falls in the morning or later in the day.
quests.explanation: Yes! Afternoon is part of the daytime.
quests.funFact: Digital clocks became popular because they're quick and easy to read at a glance!

quests.instruction: "A watch glowing softly in the dark, checked one last time before sleep" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about the phrase 'before sleep' — when does that happen?
quests.explanation: Yes! Checking a watch right before sleep happens at night.
quests.funFact: Some watches glow in the dark using a special paint that soaks up light during the day!
